flawed_step: Line 0040 assumes without justification that c(u→v)>0; the problem does not exclude zero-capacity edges.
counterexample: Let V={s,t,u,v}, with edges s→t of capacity 1 and u→v of capacity 0. Every (s,t)-cut has capacity 1 because it cuts s→t, so 1 is the minimum. The cut S={s,u}, T={v,t} is minimum and has u∈S, v∈T. The cut S′={s,v}, T′={u,t} is also minimum and has u∈T′, v∈S′. Thus both configurations exist.
assessment_summary: The claimed result is false for a standard flow network allowing nonnegative capacities. The proof’s strict inequality depends on an unstated positive-capacity assumption.
